package_info.package_name: Emotet, AZORULT, Lokibot, Grandoreiro, Agent Tesla, FormBook, HawkEye
package_info.package_manager: malspam/email delivery (not a software package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: These malware families are distributed via COVID-19-themed malspam campaigns, using social engineering to trick users into opening malicious attachments or clicking links. The payloads perform credential theft, keylogging, banking fraud, and other malicious actions, often by exploiting document macros or delivering executables disguised as legitimate files.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: VBA macro embedded in Word document that downloads and executes Emotet payload
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user opens the document and enables macros, the VBA macro executes, downloads the Emotet malware from a remote server, and runs it on the victim's machine.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Macros in unsolicited documents that download and execute code are a classic malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Word documents should not contain macros that download and execute external code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise automation uses macros, but never for downloading and running untrusted binaries.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious macro or exploit code in Word document exploiting MS Office vulnerabilities to install AZORULT
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the document is opened, the macro or exploit code runs, exploiting Office vulnerabilities to install the AZORULT infostealer, which then exfiltrates credentials and sensitive data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Office documents exploiting vulnerabilities or containing macros that install infostealers are highly suspicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate documents do not exploit vulnerabilities or install software.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; exploitation of vulnerabilities is never legitimate in this context.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Executable or script in attachment that installs Lokibot
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the attachment is opened, the executable runs and installs Lokibot, which steals credentials and exfiltrates them.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unexpected executables in email attachments are a common malware delivery vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate business emails do not send executables disguised as documents.

execution_context.trigger: user clicks malicious link in email

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious link downloads Grandoreiro banking trojan executable
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user clicks the link, a banking trojan is downloaded and executed, enabling credential theft and banking fraud.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Links in emails leading to direct downloads of executables are highly suspicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate organizations do not send links to executables in unsolicited emails.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Software vendors may send download links, but never for banking trojans.

execution_context.file_location: email attachment (executable disguised as Excel file)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Agent Tesla keylogger executable with Excel file icon
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user opens the attachment, the Agent Tesla keylogger is installed, capturing keystrokes and exfiltrating them to the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Executables disguised as documents are a classic malware trick.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Excel files are not PE executables.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; this is a deception technique.

execution_context.trigger: user opens ZIP archive and runs contained executable

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Executable in ZIP archive launches GuLoader, which installs FormBook infostealer
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user extracts and runs the executable, GuLoader downloads and installs FormBook, which steals credentials and exfiltrates them.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: ZIP archives containing executables are a common malware delivery method.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate ZIPs from trusted sources rarely contain infostealer loaders.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Software distribution, but not for infostealers.

execution_context.trigger: user opens email attachment or clicks link

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: HawkEye infostealer payload delivered via phishing email
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user interacts with the attachment or link, HawkEye infostealer is installed, capturing credentials and exfiltrating them.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Infostealer payloads delivered via phishing are a hallmark of malspam.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate emails do not deliver infostealers.

attack_chain.action: User receives COVID-19-themed phishing email with malicious attachment or link.
attack_chain.leads_to: User opens attachment or clicks link.

attack_chain.action: User opens malicious document, executable, or link.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes on victim's machine.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code downloads and installs malware payload (Emotet, AZORULT, Lokibot, Grandoreiro, Agent Tesla, FormBook, HawkEye).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware executes and begins data theft or other malicious activity.

attack_chain.action: Malware exfiltrates credentials, keystrokes, or banking information to attacker-controlled servers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive information or financial accounts.

behavioral_signatures: Office documents with macros that download and execute code
Executables disguised as documents (e.g., Excel icon)
Unexpected network connections after opening email attachments
Infostealer or keylogger process creation after document open
file_indicators: ZIP archives with single executable inside
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known C2 infrastructure for Emotet, AZORULT, Lokibot, Grandoreiro, Agent Tesla, FormBook, HawkEye
Unusual HTTP/HTTPS POST requests after opening attachments
Connections to IPs/domains associated with malware delivery
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor email gateways for COVID-19-themed phishing emails with attachments or links. Flag Office documents with macros, especially those that initiate network connections or drop executables. Detect executables masquerading as documents by checking file headers and icons. Alert on ZIP archives containing only a single executable. Monitor endpoint behavior for process creation from email clients or document viewers, especially if followed by network activity to suspicious domains. Use threat intelligence to block known C2 domains and IPs associated with these malware families.
